subject: Apollo Systems: throughput spike RCA handoff, commitments tracker, exec readout
messages:
From: Elaine Zhou <elaine@apollosystems.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@apollosystems.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Significant throughput spike causing downstream 5xxs - immediate follow-up

Kimberly —

Quick heads up: we observed a sustained throughput spike on our account starting ~08:40 PDT today that coincided with a sharp increase in 5xxs across several checkout endpoints. Error rate peaked at ~9% for ~18 minutes; our SREs had circuit-breakers trip which impacted ~6% of our customer sessions. We escalated internally and also flagged this to our Ops leadership.

Can Redwood provide an initial incident summary and ETA for a root cause analysis? The spike overwhelmed our normal retry/backoff patterns and we need to prepare an exec readout this week. Also please include any early mitigation steps you applied and whether there was a config/deployment change on Redwood's side around that time.

Attachments: grafana screenshots (we've attached two) and our quick incident log.

Thanks — we need this consolidated ASAP.

Elaine
Elaine Zhou
Head of Platform Operations, Apollo Systems
elaine@apollosystems.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Zhou <elaine@apollosystems.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@apollosystems.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Significant throughput spike causing downstream 5xxs - immediate follow-up

Hi Elaine / Carlos —

Thanks for the alert and the Grafana captures. I'm sorry for the disruption — we take incidents like this very seriously. Marcus (SRE lead) is on the thread and has started an initial investigation. High level:

- We have a running incident channel and are collecting traces and server metrics.
- Initial indicators point to a sudden shift in request burst distribution that exposed a KV-cache cold-path on one model shard cluster; that path has higher P99 latency under burst.
- We have an on-call mitigation in place to route traffic to a warm shard set; engineering is continuing validation.

Next steps (short):
1) Marcus will share a short incident timeline and any immediate mitigations applied.
2) We'll produce an RCA and a remediation register by Friday EOD with owner assignments and target dates.
3) We can schedule an executive readout — Kimberly/Marcus and I can join; propose Thu 3/25 09:00 PDT or Fri 3/26 13:00 PDT. Please confirm preferred slot.

I will attach interim logs and a one-page summary as soon as Marcus posts them.

Best,
Kimberly Park
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: (internal)
Date: 2028-03-24T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: [Internal] Draft RCA + action register (Apollo throughput spike)

Team —

I've attached the first-pass RCA (apollo_throughput_rca_v1.pdf) and started the action tracker (remediation_action_register.xlsx). Summary below:

Incident timeline (short):
- 08:37 PDT: small burst observed; autoscaler responded as expected.
- 08:40 PDT: non-uniform routing caused ~60% of traffic to land on a single shard group; that group experienced KV-cache misses which pushed requests to a slower cold path and caused tail latency to spike.
- 08:58 PDT: automated fallback routing triggered; we manually accelerated rollout of routing patch at 09:05 PDT and traffic normalized by 09:12 PDT.

Root causes (multi-factor):
1) Scheduler mis-weighting during a transient autoscale event (primary)
2) A model shard with suboptimal KV cache warmup behavior under burst (secondary)
3) Insufficient canary monitoring for cross-shard imbalance (process gap)

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Forced redistribution to healthy shard group (manual rollback of ill-performing routing weight).
- Throttled aggressive autoscale ramp for the affected pool for 30 minutes.

Top remediation items (from tracker):
- R1: Fix scheduler weight calculation and add guardrail tests (owner: Karthik, target: 2028-04-05)
- R2: Improve KV cache warmup and add synthetic warmup traffic to autoscaler flow (owner: Marcus, target: 2028-04-12)
- R3: Add cross-shard imbalance alerting and dashboard (owner: Grace, target: 2028-03-30)
- R4: Customer comms and credits proposal (owner: Kimberly, target: 2028-03-29)

Notes for exec readout: focus on cause -> containment -> remediation -> timeline + follow-through (we've linked the tracker to the jira ticket JIRA-SRE-7893).

Attachments: apollo_throughput_rca_v1.pdf, remediation_action_register.xlsx, grafana_spike_dashboard.png

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-24T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Internal] Draft RCA + action register (Apollo throughput spike)

Thanks Marcus — solid first pass. Two quick edits for the exec slide:

- Consolidate the timeline to 3 bullets (detected / mitigated / normalized) with absolute timestamps and customer impact metric (sessions affected ~6%).
- Add a single "what we're changing" slide with R1-R3 and clear owner/T- shirt sizing (S/M/L).

I've updated the tracker with the dashboard ticket and added a follow-up check-in for 04/12 to validate KV warmup metrics. Also propose we offer a one-time credit equivalent to two hours of throughput consumption while we close R2 (tracked under R4).

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Reliability Programs
grace@redwood.com

Kimberly / Marcus —

Thanks for the RCA and the proposed action plan. A few asks from Apollo's side before the exec readout:
- Can you confirm the estimated ETA for R2 (KV warmup fixes) and whether it will require any scheduled changes on our side?
- We want detail on the credit proposal and how it will be applied to our invoice.
- Please share the exec slide deck at least 2 hours before the readout.

We'll take Thu 3/25 09:00 PDT for the readout. Elaine and I will join along with our CTO.

Carlos

c.ruiz@apollosystems.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Zhou <elaine@apollosystems.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@apollosystems.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: commitments, credits, and next checkpoints (Apollo)

Elaine / Carlos —

Appreciate the conversation on Thursday. Per the readout and internal tracker, summary of commitments and next checkpoints:

- R1 (scheduler weight fix): Karthik, target 2028-04-05. Code change will be backward compatible; no action required from Apollo.
- R2 (KV warmup / synthetic warmup traffic): Marcus, target 2028-04-12. We will run controlled warmup in our staging pool and validate—no customer config change expected.
- R3 (cross-shard alerting + dashboard): Grace, target 2028-03-30. We will share dashboard link once live.
- R4 (credits): Kimberly, committed to a one-time invoice credit equivalent to two peak-hours of throughput consumption; finance will issue a credit note by 2028-04-02 and apply to the next invoice cycle.

Action items assigned are all in the remediation_action_register.xlsx (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRCA). We'll update that tracker weekly until all items are closed and will schedule a validation check on 2028-04-13 to confirm R2 behaviour in production.

If anything changes, we'll ping this thread. Thanks again for the constructive partnership — we know incidents like this are painful and are committed to preventing recurrence.

Best,
Kimberly Park
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
